source.title: Models & Pricing
source.peakExclusions: Chinese public holidays are off-peak in full at the source; the snapshot cannot know them and prices them as peak, which only overstates.

changesSincePrecheck20260821: Flash was renamed deepseek-flash and moved to DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash; the page says the legacy names are still accepted but their models are retired, and the announcement says they route there temporarily.
Flash rates fell, effective 04:00 UTC on 2026-09-10 per the announcement.

The snapshot now models the page's Monday-to-Friday peak rule; weekends and Chinese public holidays are off-peak in full. The 2026-08-21 record captured no weekday rule, and this record does not establish when the rule began.

Pro: the pricing page lists deepseek-v4-pro as DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 at unchanged rates. The announcement says all deepseek-v4-pro requests route to V4.1-Flash at Flash rates from 04:00 UTC on 2026-09-14 until V4.1-Pro launches. Archived copies of the pricing page from 2026-09-11 16:55 UTC to 2026-09-17 carried a note reversing that (service continues after 2026-09-14 with billing unchanged); the live page no longer carries it. The snapshot keeps the page's Pro rates, which can only overstate a Pro run.
decision: The official public page matched every Flash/Pro rate, peak window, peak weekday rule, currency, unit and the renamed Flash model id in the dated repository snapshot. This precheck does not pass the release reconciliation: no authenticated GET /models was observed, so whether deepseek-flash is visible to a real key is unconfirmed; the official sources disagree on which model serves deepseek-v4-pro, which only the returned model id of a real call can settle; and requested/returned model IDs, aggregate usage, Provider billing, preview-origin CORS and credential revocation still require the bounded real canary.
